title: Preparation of Light-responsive Membranes by a Combined Surface Grafting and Postmodification Process
protocol: Dissolve HEMA (100 ml; 0.718 mol) in 200 ml water.
Wash the aqueous phase 3 times with hexane (100 ml) using a separating funnel.
Saturate the aqueous phase with sodium chloride and extract HEMA with diethyl ether (50 ml).
Dry the organic phase over MgSO4.
Remove the solvent in vacuo (100 mbar, 40 °C).
Distill the HEMA under reduced pressure (15 mbar; 99 °C).
Prepare a 0.62 M methanolic solution of inhibitor-free HEMA.
Pour 30 ml of the solution into a one-necked flask.
Eliminate oxygen by bubbling Ar through the solution for 1 hour.
Position two polycarbonate membranes next to each other in the plasma chamber.
Place the shiny side of the membrane towards the gas phase.
Connect the plasma chamber to a high vacuum (20 mbar) and evacuate for 5 minutes.
Close the valve to the vacuum and open the valve connected to argon and oxygen gas mixture.
Purge the chamber with argon (15 sccm) and oxygen (2.5 sccm) for 2 hours.
Initiate the plasma and reduce power to 12 W for polycarbonate membrane treatment.
Treat membranes with plasma for 4 minutes.
Connect the monomer solution with the chamber by opening the corresponding valve.
Switch off the plasma and evacuate the chamber.
Connect the monomer solution with the chamber by opening the corresponding valve and pouring the solution into the chamber.
Ensure that the membranes are covered with the monomer solution.
Open the valve connected to argon and store the reaction mixture for 12 hours at 20 °C.
Remove the monomer solution from the chamber.
Wash the membranes with methanol in an ultrasonic bath for 5 minutes.
Repeat the washing procedure with water.
Dry the membrane in vacuo over molecular sieves for 2 hours.

Prepare a solution of spirobenzopyran 1 (100 mg; 0.27 mmol), N,N-dicyclohexylcarbodiimide (DCC) (55 mg; 0.27 mmol), and dimethylaminopyridine (DMAP) (33 mg, 0.27 mmol) in tert-butylmethylether (TBME) (12 ml).
Pour the solution into a round-bottom flask dried with argon.
Add the coated membrane to the solution and stir gently at room temperature for 12 hours.
Remove the solution from the membrane.
Wash the membrane with tert-butylmethylether in an ultrasonic bath for 5 minutes.
Repeat the washing procedure with ethanol and water.
Dry the membrane in vacuo over molecular sieves for 2 hours.
Fix the membrane with a standard tape on a metal O-ring.
Position a drop of nanopure water (3.3 μl) on that part of the membrane surface, which is not in contact with the O-ring.
Measure the contact angle at 5 different spots of the membrane.
Measure contact angles at three different spots of the membranes after 0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 14, and 21 days.
Fill the receptor chamber of the Franz diffusion cell with water (12 ml).
Fix the membrane in a Franz diffusion cell.
Ensure that the membrane is in contact with the water of the receptor chamber.
Fill the donor chamber with an aqueous caffeine solution (20 mM; 3.0 ml).
Irradiate the membrane from the top of the donor chamber with white-light.
Collect samples (200 μl) from the receptor cell every 10 min for track-edged polycarbonate membranes with a pore diameter of 200 nm.
Repeat the experiment but irradiate the membrane with UV-light (366 nm, 80 W/m2) during the entire permeability test.
Plot a calibration curve with 15 different caffeine concentrations (between 0.05 mg/ml and 1.5 mM/L) using a UV/Vis spectrometer.
Calibrate at 293 nm.
Determine the concentration of each collected sample using the calibration curve.
Plot the determined concentration vs. the time of the collected samples.
Make a linear fit through the points and determine Δc from the slope.
